clue.text: Where children are taught to get on?

definitions.text: Where children are taught to get on?

parts.words: Where children are taught to get on?
parts.note: read as a place where pupils learn to climb aboard trains and buses; really a school where pupils live in term time

explanation.surface: A question about the kind of school that teaches children to get along in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on' suggests getting on in life or getting along with others; the cryptic reading is boarding, as in climbing on to a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A residential school where pupils lodge during term, the boarding being the pun on getting aboard.

clue.text: Dog wanted to lie alongside miner endlessly

parts.note: to border something is to lie alongside it

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the miner word is dropped

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner

explanation.surface: A dog wished to lie down next to a coal miner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog wanted' looks like a request; 'wanted' merely links. COLLIER, a coal miner, loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Border collie is a sheepdog breed from the Anglo-Scottish border region.

clue.text: Bill races one into the room

indicators.note: into means the races and one are placed inside the bill

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
the TT races are motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Bill rushes someone into the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is not a man but AC, account; TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle races.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is a room in the roof space at the top of a house.

clue.text: Having spread dais with soft fruit, vanish

indicators.note: spread means the dais letters are spread out into a new order

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for soft
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Having spread fruit on the platform, someone disappears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges DAIS into DISA; P is the musical abbreviation for soft.
explanation.definitionFit: To disappear is to pass out of sight, a direct synonym of vanish.

clue.text: Turned on crazy crossword compiler caught wandering

indicators.note: turned means the word on is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: mad means crazy
the setter refers to themselves as I
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone turned on a mad setter who was caught roaming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' reverses ON to NO; the compiler of the crossword is the setter, I.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic peoples travel from place to place, so it means roaming or wandering.

clue.text: Save cruel student being imprisoned

indicators.note: being imprisoned means the student is shut inside the cruel word

parts.note: savage means cruel
L is a learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: Rescue a student being locked up by a brutal regime.
explanation.walkthrough: L, the learner plate, stands for a student and is locked inside SAVAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To salvage something is to rescue it from loss, so to save it.

clue.text: Shy dropout hiding in special hotel

indicators.note: hiding in tells us the answer is concealed within the letters of the words shy dropout

explanation.surface: A timid dropout hides away in a special hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: A hydro is a British hotel offering spa or hydropathic treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydro is a hotel with spa facilities offering water cures, hence a special kind of hotel.

clue.text: Shades one entering closed back street

parts.note: something closed is finished, over

indicators.note: entering means one goes inside the reversed street abbreviation
back means the street abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: Shadows fall on someone going into a closed back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the street abbreviation round to TS; 'entering' puts the one inside it, giving TONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtones are subtle hints or nuances, which shades of meaning also are.

clue.text: First religious site specially designed for ceremonies

indicators.note: first tells us to take only the opening letter of the word religious
something specially designed has been rearranged into a new form, so the letters of site are reshuffled

explanation.surface: The first religious site was purpose-built for holding ceremonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' looks like an ordinal for the site but picks only the opening letter of 'religious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rites are formal religious or solemn ceremonies, so the plural nouns match exactly.

clue.text: Complaints made when old lady goes to toilet?

parts.note: an old lady is slang for one's mother, MA
the ladies is a British name for a women's public toilet

explanation.surface: Ailments that arise when an elderly woman visits the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old lady' is slang for mother, giving MA; 'goes to' simply joins her to the toilet, the LADIES, a common British name for the women's lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladies are illnesses, and complaints is a standard word for ailments of the body.

clue.text: Lie back before pushing point into floor

indicators.note: before places the support word ahead of the next piece

parts.note: to back someone is to second or support them

indicators.note: pushing means the point is forced into the lie word

parts.note: a story is a lie
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Lean back before pushing a point into the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie back' looks like relaxing, but 'back' is to support, as when you second a motion. 'pushing ... into' puts E (east) in the lie word.
explanation.definitionFit: The second storey is a level of a building, a floor.

clue.text: Bolted relief valve to an old copper

parts.note: an escape valve releases pressure, so a relief valve can be called an escape
d was the abbreviation for an old British penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: Someone fastened a pressure-release valve onto an ancient copper vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolted' looks like 'fastened' but means ran off. D stood for the pre-1971 British penny, a copper coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt is to run away suddenly, so bolted and escaped are past-tense synonyms.

clue.text: Appointment accepted by stout preacher

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside, so the appointment goes within the stout

parts.note: stout is a dark beer, a kind of ale
a post is a job or appointment

explanation.surface: A job is offered to a plump clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' reads as an adjective for the preacher but is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle was one sent out to spread the Gospel, so a preacher or missionary.

clue.text: Patient starts talking in class

indicators.note: in places the opening letter of talking within the word for a patient

parts.note: a doctor's patient is referred to as a case

indicators.note: starts tells us to take the opening letter of talking

explanation.surface: A patient begins to speak during a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like an adjective but is a noun, a medical CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, especially in the Hindu system.

clue.text: Layers of earth under a bus start shaking

indicators.note: shaking means the letters of a bus start are jumbled up

explanation.surface: The ground layers beneath a bus tremble as it starts up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' rearranges A BUS START. 'under' belongs to the definition: substrata lie beneath the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Substrata are underlying layers of rock or soil beneath the surface strata.

clue.text: Endless street party gradually getting louder

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the street word is cut off

parts.note: a crescent is a curved street
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A street party goes on and on, getting noisier.
explanation.walkthrough: A CRESCENT is a curved street of houses; DO is British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Crescendo is the musical term for a passage that steadily increases in volume.

clue.text: Lieutenant admittedly against leading Italian singers

indicators.note: admittedly is read as admitted, taken in, so the lieutenant goes inside

parts.note: contra is Latin for against

indicators.note: leading means the first letter of Italian

explanation.surface: A lieutenant admits to opposing the top Italian singers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admittedly' is read as 'admitted', taking the lieutenant inside. Contralti is the Italian plural of contralto.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraltos are female singers with the lowest voice, and contralti is the Italian plural.

clue.text: Putting tar in our silo turned out to be tedious

indicators.note: in places the sailor within the rearranged letters
turned out suggests the letters of our silo have been tipped over into a new order

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

explanation.surface: Coating the inside of our silo with tar proved a tiresome job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges OUR SILO into LORIOUS, and AB, a tar or sailor, goes inside after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Laborious work demands great effort and drags on, so it is tedious or wearisome.

clue.text: Go on too long before function's finished

indicators.note: before places the finished word ahead of the function word

parts.note: something finished is over
a run is a function, as when a machine is running

explanation.surface: A meeting overshoots before the event is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' suggests a social event; here it is RUN, as a machine functions.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting that overruns goes on beyond its planned time.

clue.text: Waves on lake damaged plant growing near the coast

parts.note: the waves are the sea

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of lake are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Waves hitting the lake harm a coastal plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges LAKE into KALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea kale is a cabbage-family plant found growing wild on beaches.

clue.text: Was Inquisitive boy rejected by top journalist?

indicators.note: rejected suggests being sent back, so the boy word is read backwards

parts.note: a boy is a son
ED is short for editor, the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: Was the curious lad turned away by the editor?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the boy word round; ED, editor, is the senior journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose about is to pry, so nosed means was nosy or inquisitive.

clue.text: Is having name and number inserted on key excessive?

indicators.note: having means holding, so the word is contains the name and number

parts.note: ten is a number
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A question about whether adding a name and number to a key is going too far.
explanation.walkthrough: IS holds N and TEN, giving INTENS, then 'on' adds E, a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense can mean extreme or of excessive degree, as in intense heat.

clue.text: Cut a large amount up before church

indicators.note: before puts the reversed amount ahead of church
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a ton is a large amount

explanation.surface: A big amount is cut before reaching the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TON to NOT in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small V-shaped cut in an edge or surface.

clue.text: Entertainer needing car repaired to ring club

indicators.note: repaired suggests the car is put back together differently, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ring is O-shaped
a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.surface: A performer has to get the car fixed to call a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' rearranges CAR into ACR; 'ring' is the letter O, not a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat performs gymnastic feats in a circus, a kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Refuse to go here having turned up, say, for a spree

parts.note: a bin is where rubbish goes

indicators.note: turned up means read upward, backwards, in a down clue

parts.note: EG means for example, say

explanation.surface: Rubbish turned up where it should go, ready for a spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is rubbish; 'turned up' reverses the abbreviation for 'say' in this down clue, giving GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a bout of excessive indulgence, a spree.

clue.text: Tossing a caber? It could be a cause of disease!

indicators.note: tossing suggests throwing the letters about, so a caber and it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Highland games competitor wonders whether tossing the caber could make one ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Caber tossing is a Scottish Highland games event in which a long pole is thrown end over end. 'Tossing' rearranges A CABER and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria are microbes, some of which are germs that cause illness.

clue.text: Individualist takes one in both hands

indicators.note: in tells us one goes within the two hand letters

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, both hands

explanation.surface: An independent person takes one in both hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both hands' gives L and R, left and right, with ONE between.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner keeps to themselves, preferring their own company, an individualist.

clue.text: Way of paying if transporting dray on vehicles

indicators.note: transporting means carrying the letters elsewhere, so dray on vehicles is rearranged

explanation.surface: A method of payment for moving a brewer's cart on lorries.
explanation.walkthrough: A dray is a low cart for carrying beer barrels. 'transporting' rearranges DRAY ON VEHICLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying the courier when goods arrive is a recognised method of payment.
